new_entities.name: Early rhythm control for atrial fibrillation
aliases: early antiarrhythmic or ablation strategy in AF
rhythm control within 1 year of AF diagnosis
new_entities.description: Structured rhythm-control treatment started early after atrial fibrillation diagnosis, using antiarrhythmic drugs, cardioversion, or ablation.

new_entities.name: Cardiovascular outcomes
new_entities.description: Composite cardiovascular outcomes such as cardiovascular death, stroke, heart-failure hospitalization, or acute coronary syndrome.

edges.effect_quant: EAST-AFNET 4 showed fewer first primary cardiovascular events with early rhythm control than usual care (HR 0.79). Real-world meta-analysis also found lower composite cardiovascular events (HR 0.86), and high-comorbidity EAST-AFNET 4 patients had an even larger benefit (HR 0.64).
edges.population: adults with recently diagnosed atrial fibrillation, especially those with cardiovascular risk factors or higher comorbidity burden
edges.mechanism: Starting rhythm control before prolonged atrial remodeling may maintain sinus rhythm, reduce AF burden, and prevent downstream stroke, heart-failure worsening, and other cardiovascular decompensation.
edges.summary: This is one of the clearest examples where earlier intervention changed the old rate-versus-rhythm story. The benefit is not just symptom relief; earlier rhythm control lowers major cardiovascular events in appropriately selected recently diagnosed AF populations.
edges.caveats: The strategy effect is strongest when treatment starts within the first year after diagnosis and in patients with meaningful cardiovascular risk. The evidence reflects a strategy that can include drugs, cardioversion, or ablation rather than a single intervention.

evidence.citation: Kirchhof P et al 2020 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Early Rhythm-Control Therapy in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation. EAST-AFNET 4.

effect_quant.comparator: first primary cardiovascular outcome in EAST-AFNET 4 with early rhythm control versus usual care

evidence.citation: Zhu W et al 2024 Int J Cardiol
evidence.notes: Real-world evidence of early rhythm control in patients with atrial fibrillation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: primary composite cardiovascular outcome with early rhythm control versus rate control in real-world studies

evidence.notes: Early Rhythm Control in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and High Comorbidity Burden.
